thread:
andrew: Noticed a spike in CPU on host-proxy during the 04:00 UTC canary. Latency p95 for small streaming responses jumped ~40ms. Profiling points to tokenization + http2 frame handling on the proxy host.

maya: Yikes. Was this after the kernel-selection change yesterday?

andrew: Nope, that change landed earlier and looked fine. This started after the streaming chunk coalescer tweak (reduce min-chunk to 128B) — looks like we now create a lot more tiny frames. Flamegraphs show disproportionate time in our JS tokenizer and grpc/http2 read loops.

sam: Can you paste the flame snippet?

andrew: paste:
```
  host-proxy (cpu)
  ├─ http2::read_frame
  │  ├─ frame_parse::headers (18%)
  │  └─ frame_parse::data (12%)
  ├─ tokenize::run_tokenizer (26%)
  │  └─ tokenize::utf8_scan (14%)
  └─ stream_coalescer::emit_small_chunk (9%)
```

olga: Small frame churn + tokenizer on hot path = two problems: syscall/packet overhead and repeated allocations. If every 128B chunk gets tokenized separately we lose batching on both host and GPU. Also KV cache keys change if prefix boundaries differ, which could cause KV thrash.

maya: Agreed. Hypothesis: the coalescer change improved latency for very small responses but regresses CPU and cache hit-rate overall. We should measure: 1) per-request tokenization calls, 2) KV cache hit-rate pre/post.

sam: I ran a quick throughput test on canary with `wrk` and captured counters. Tokenizer calls per request up ~3x, KV cache hits down ~12%. Logs attached to the thread (link): https://redwood.internal/logs/ingress/1837654321

andrew: Thanks. Quick mitigations: roll back min-chunk to 512B, and add a short-path in proxy to do zero-copy header parsing for known routes. Can we try both in canary?

olga: Zero-copy header parsing PR ready: `olga/zcopy-headers`. It avoids copying bytes into the tokenizer for the common JSON streaming content-type and only parses data frames after we've buffered >= 512B. Should reduce UTF-8 scan calls.

kevin: Also consider moving tokenization off the network thread into a bounded worker pool so the http2 read loop isn't blocked by heavy UTF-8 scans. We did this in ingress-v1 with good results.

maya: Good idea. I'd rather start with config changes (min-chunk rollback) + deploy `olga/zcopy-headers` to canary, then measure. Worker-pool is slightly bigger refactor.

andrew: Plan:
- roll canary to previous coalescer config (min-chunk 512B) at 18:10 UTC
- deploy `olga/zcopy-headers` to canary at 18:15
- collect flamegraphs + KV cache hit-rate for a 30m window
- if CPU p95 improves and hits recover, promote to production; otherwise, enqueue worker-pool refactor and investigate batching heuristics.

ci-bot: Build succeeded for `olga/zcopy-headers` (CI #4523).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: `proxy-service` -> canary (revision: 7f3b2a).

sam: Early numbers after the rollback + zcopy deploy (10m window): CPU p95 down 28ms, tokenizer calls per request down 2.1x, KV cache hits up ~9%. Still ~6ms residual overhead from http2 frame assembly.

olga: That residual probably from gRPC marshaling path. We can optimize by skipping header canonicalization for internal calls and tuning the tcp read buffer size. I'll open a follow-up PR for header-canonicalization-skip and a tcp-tuning experiment.

kevin: For longer-term: we should tune batching heuristics to consider host-side cost. Our current heuristic only targets GPU utilization and latency; it should incorporate tokenization and per-request parse cost to pick when to join requests into a batch. I can draft a proposal.

andrew: Please do. Also add a regression test in perf-ci that runs microbench for small streaming responses and tracks tokenizer calls and KV hit-rate as first-class metrics. If either deviates by more than 10% we block the change.

maya: Noted. I'll add perf-ci gating. Good triage team, thanks. :thumbsup:

andrew: Leaving the thread open for the follow-up PRs and results. If anyone sees new spikes, @andrew @maya please ping.

kevin: I'll start the batching-heuristic RFC tomorrow and link it here.

olga: Filed follow-up: https://redwood.internal/pull/6789 (header-canonicalization-skip).

sam: Saved flamegraphs and counters to the incident folder: /incidents/2026-03-18/1837654321.

andrew: End of thread for now.
